figures.caption: Figure 1. Open in a new tab Change in MME from a knee flexion angle of 0° ( a ) to 90° ( b ) in a healthy adult. The medial meniscus that is slightly extruded at a knee flexion angle of 0° is retracted into the joint by knee flexion, at which point the extrusion disappears. MM is indicated by the dotted line. MCL medial collateral ligament, MME medial meniscal extrusion, MM medial meniscus.
Figure 2. Open in a new tab The flow chart of inclusion criteria and grouping in this study. MME medial meniscal extrusion.
Figure 3. Open in a new tab Methods for evaluating MME via coronal plane MRI. MME medial meniscal extrusion, MRI magnetic resonance imaging.

Figure 4. Open in a new tab Ultrasonographic evaluations in the supine position at knee flexion angles of ( a ) 0° and ( b ) 90°. The appropriate probe position during MME evaluation ( c ). The femoral medial epicondyle was designated as a bony landmark (asterisk), and the proximal part of the probe was installed just behind it. MME medial meniscal extrusion.

Figure 5. Open in a new tab Methods for evaluating MME via ultrasonography using longitudinal sections parallel to the MCL. MCL medial collateral ligament, MME medial meniscal extrusion, MM medial meniscus.

Figure 6. Open in a new tab Difference in MME between 0° and 90° of knee flexion. Representative case in group D: ( a ) 0° and ( b ) 90°. Representative case in group N: ( c ) 0° and ( d ) 90°. The MME of each figure: ( a ) 3.5, ( b ) 0.5, ( c ) 3.6, and ( d ) 3.0 mm. MM is indicated by the dotted line. MCL medial collateral ligament, MME medial meniscal extrusion, MM medial meniscus.
